seamRepair.prompt:
Precise seam repair only. Reference 1 is the original AI-extended aerial panorama after a reversible horizontal cyclic shift of half the width. Its defective original wrap seam is therefore exposed as a conspicuous straight vertical cut DOWN THE EXACT CENTER: misaligned tree belts, roads and field boundaries meet there. Repair that central join. Reference 2 is Sciacchitano's original 1967 aerial photo of Quang Tri looking south; it protects factual source-view layout, not invented detail. The genuine-source front view has temporarily been split between the outer edges of reference 1. Output remains an AI-processed illustration, never archival evidence.

Make the central seam disappear by creating one coherent, restrained piece of aerial farmland across a band centered on that cut. Match each side's tree belts, small roads, irrigation margins, field boundaries, horizon and grain so they form a continuous landscape. Repaint the narrow central region only; preserve reference 1 outside approximately a 400px-wide center band on the 1774px-wide image as much as possible. No blur stripe, fog wall, flat-color strip, divider, copying/mirroring of landmarks, or artificial symmetric rows. This unseen rear landscape is inferred and has no geographic accuracy claim.

Crucially do not redesign the rest of the panorama. Preserve the elevated camera, visible citadel footprint and internal buildings, moat, river, bridge and city grid near the outer edges of the shifted reference. Same 1967 setting, grayscale film texture and tone, sky, horizon height, perspective, full spherical coverage and exact 2:1 framing. Do not reproject, resize contents, crop, zoom, rotate the scene or move objects. The caller will keep only this center repair patch and undo the cyclic shift, preserving unchanged original native pixels elsewhere.

Return ONE full panorama in THIS SHIFTED orientation, ideally 1774×887 as reference 1. No text, labels, borders, frames, panels, watermarks, people, cars, military vehicles, aircraft, battle, smoke, contemporary memorials, rubble or new named historical landmarks. Only repair the visible center cut.
seamRepair.composition: ImageMagick CopyOpacity then Over; linear alpha ramps only; no other synthesis, painting or color treatment.

preservation.comparedAgainst: original generated native, not the historical source photograph

diagnostic.metric: Mean absolute RGB jump between last and first columns; terrain rows 350 inclusive to 800 exclusive; lower is better, not a historical or geometric accuracy score

seamRepair.visualInspection: Large geography cut removed; faint field-line join remains. Root inspected corrected native and rear QA crop and accepted this bounded improvement. No further image editing.

derivatives.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene, source-based panoramic outpainting.
Asset type: full spherical 360 degree equirectangular photographic panorama for an educational Quang Tri viewer.
Input image 1 is the historical edit target and factual visual anchor: Sciacchitano's black-and-white aerial photograph of Quang Tri citadel and city looking south, autumn 1967. Its source is https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:34._Quang_Tri_Citadel_and_City_looking_South_Fall_1967.jpg and it is CC BY-SA 3.0. This request creates an AI extrapolation, not an authentic archival photograph or a measured reconstruction.

Extend that actual source view into ONE exact 2:1 equirectangular full sphere, 360 degrees horizontally and 180 vertically. Highest native resolution available; target 4096 by 2048 if supported, otherwise the largest exact 2:1 size. Output only the full rectangular panorama, no inset or side-by-side panels.
Camera stays airborne above Quang Tri, matching the input elevated southward view. Place the source's photographed layout in the center-front downward-looking sector around latitude -25 to -45 degrees. Preserve the clearly visible rectilinear citadel footprint, moat, internal low buildings, street grid, river and bridge, the proportions and relative positions of those photographed features. Do not relocate the camera to ground level. Do not add or change named landmarks. Only extend beyond the existing photograph with restrained plausible flat central-Vietnam terrain: low scattered rooflines, fields, water margins, trees and distant haze. These unseen sides and the rear are explicitly inferential; keep them visually quiet and avoid asserting detailed new architecture.

Projection: a genuine full equirectangular texture suitable for a sphere. Horizon at the vertical midpoint, continuous pale sky in upper hemisphere; terrain in lower hemisphere seen from this same elevated camera. Top edge tends to uniform zenith sky; bottom edge tends toward straight-down land texture. Left and right edges meet seamlessly with identical horizon height and exposure, no duplicated prominent landmark at the seam, no pinching.
Monochrome grayscale throughout with restrained period-film grain and soft photographic contrast matching the source, ordinary diffuse daylight. Depict 1967 intact town conditions visible in the source; no invented 1972 destruction.
Avoid absolutely: writing, labels, dates, captions, archival stamps, frames, borders, white margins, watermarks, annotation crosses, logos, aircraft or aircraft parts, soldiers, crowds, cars, military vehicles, battles, smoke, explosions, corpses, blood, contemporary monuments, modern high-rises, modern roads or tourist infrastructure. Do not present this extrapolation as source evidence.
derivatives.modifications: Spherical reconstruction and outpainting from the credited photograph. The rear join was repaired with a 400-pixel generated strip and 64-pixel feather overlaps on a cyclically rolled native texture; pixels outside this strip were retained.
